hints.title: Subproblem Conflict Constraint
hints.text: A subset is invalid if it contains any two elements with difference equal to k.

hints.title: Frequency-Based Pruning
hints.text: Maintain a frequency counter of chosen elements. A number x can be added if x - k and x + k are currently absent.

hints.title: Excluding Empty Set
hints.text: Explore all subsets using decision branching and subtract 1 from the total valid subset count to exclude the empty subset.

hints.title: Backtracking Conflict Check Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def beautifulSubsets(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        from collections import defaultdict
        nums.sort()
        count = defaultdict(int)
        ans = 0
        def backtrack(i):
            nonlocal ans
            if i == len(nums):
                ans += 1
                return
            backtrack(i + 1)
            if count[nums[i] - k] == 0:
                count[nums[i]] += 1
                backtrack(i + 1)
                count[nums[i]] -= 1
        backtrack(0)
        return ans - 1
```

complexity.notes: Backtracking branches twice per element; n <= 20 ensures at most 2^20 operations.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Brute force generating all subsets and checking pairwise differences takes O(n^2 * 2^n).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n) recursion stack and frequency map.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Sorts and prunes with frequency map or groups by modulo remainder.
